# 127 — Xinhua: UHV power expressway (Xinjiang to economic hubs)

- **URL:** https://english.news.cn/20260113/3e3a7d6df5744fefb18b98fa31a4addb/c.html
- **Publisher:** Xinhua (Xinhua Headlines)
- **Published:** 2026-01-13
- **Fetched:** 2026-09-14
- **Authoritative:** yes (state wire service; primary source for the UHV-network claim)

## Key facts recovered

- UHV = ultra-high-voltage transmission; defined as AC ≥ 1000 kV and DC ≥ ±800 kV.
- Three UHV DC lines from Xinjiang account for **over 90%** of the region's outbound power transmission.
- Part of a nationwide network of **42 UHV lines** bridging western energy deposits (coal, wind, solar, hydrogen) with central/eastern load centers.
- Since 2010 Xinjiang transmitted **over 1 trillion kWh** to **22 provincial regions**; one-third of kWh from renewables (climate benefit ≈ 13 billion trees).
- **Changji–Guquan ±1100 kV** UHV DC line (launched Sept 2019) links far-west Xinjiang with the eastern powerhouse.
- Hami–Chongqing ±800 kV line (June 2025); Hami South–Zhengzhou line (Jan 2014).
- Receiving end: ~20% of Anhui's electricity now from Xinjiang; ~10% of Henan's peak demand met by Xinjiang power.

## Verification notes / discrepancies

- The fetched Xinhua article confirms the **42 UHV lines** and the **Changji–Guquan ±1100 kV** line.
- The draft's Source-127 parenthetical claims "22 AC + 20 DC, ~370 GW inter-regional capacity" and "Changji–Guquan ~3,300 km" — these specific sub-figures (22+20 split, 370 GW, 3,300 km, 12 GW, Jiuquan–Xiangtan 2,383 km) are **NOT present in the fetched Xinhua text**. They appear to come from a different Xinhua/State Grid source. Flagged: the 42-line count and ±1100 kV Changji–Guquan are corroborated; the AC/DC split, GW capacity, and exact km figures are not re-verified against this URL.
